chapters.title: Select a Model and Access Posture

figures.alt: Five access booths expose different model-control, inspection, hosting, adaptation, and operations surfaces.
figures.evidenceRole: Supports responsibility distribution without declaring a universally superior posture.

figures.alt: Candidates occupy a constraint frontier after hard gates remove ineligible options.
figures.evidenceRole: Operationalizes task-specific selection; it is not measured candidate performance.

figures.alt: A lockbox binds all behavior-facing versions into one baseline identity.
figures.evidenceRole: Defines manifest completeness without claiming bitwise determinism.

figures.alt: Repeated trials from one configuration occupy a visible variation band.
figures.evidenceRole: Separates repeated observations from configuration change without prescribing a distribution.

figures.alt: Trusted control and authorized intent remain separate from untrusted case and evidence content.
figures.evidenceRole: Supports the semantic trust boundary but does not claim separation alone prevents attacks.

figures.alt: One instruction module changes while model, cases, adapter, decoding, and evaluator stay fixed.
figures.evidenceRole: Illustrates controlled ablation without claiming a measured improvement.

limitations: Mosaic Desk, every candidate, every result, and every adversarial fixture in this batch are fictional and synthetic.
The conditional access selection is a decision-mechanics fixture, not a provider recommendation or approval.
The baseline proves deterministic software-contract mechanics, not live language-model quality or determinism.
Message separation and delimiters are necessary engineering structures, not complete prompt-injection defenses.
Figure records are semantic anchors only; no image asset exists until root runs ImageGen.
Managed and open-weight paths share behavior evidence requirements while retaining different unknowns and operational responsibilities.
